sections.h2: Who does what at the Fiscal Office
sections.html:
Within the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office, three units shape a homeowner's tax life. Appraisal puts a value on every parcel. Complaints about that value go to the Board of Revision. The Treasurer's Office mails the bill and invests what it collects. The Fiscal Office also runs Real Property for credits and charges, a Budget Commission that sets rates, Delinquent Tax Outreach, and a Transfer and Recording unit that keeps property records, with documents available from 1810 forward.

Everything sits in the county's Administrative Building, a single stop for most errands, 2079 East 9th Street in Cleveland. Transfer and Recording is on the 4th floor, Appraisal on the 3rd, the Board of Revision on the 2nd and the Treasurer on the 1st. The number for land records, appraisals and the Fiscal Office is 216-443-7420.

sections.h2: Due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes in two installments and runs a year behind. Payments are due in mid-February and mid-August, so taxes accrued in one year are paid the next. Manufactured home tax is billed for the current year, with payments due in early March and late August. Owners can enroll in EasyPay to prepay future bills, or in E-Billing to get bills by email or text.

Way to payCost and rules
OnlineNo fee for e-check; debit card is a flat $2.95; credit card is 2.3% with a $1.50 minimum
Phone1-877-738-1212, with an asterisk standing in for each space in the parcel number
In personFirst-floor cashier at 2079 East 9th Street, open only in collection season: January and February, then July and August
MailPO Box 94547, Cleveland, OH 44101, checks or money orders only
Drop boxOutside the Administrative Building, checks or money orders only

A postmark shows when postal machinery handled the envelope, and that can be later than the day you mailed it. Ohio law relies on the postmark, so if the deadline is near, mail early, get a hand-stamped postmark at the counter, or choose another method.

sections.h2: Late payment, penalties and payment plans
sections.html:
A late half costs ten percent of the unpaid balance under Ohio Revised Code 323.121, and delinquent taxes also gather interest at the rate set under section 5703.47. If the full amount comes in inside ten days of the deadline, the penalty is halved. A valid delinquent tax contract stops further interest while it stays in force, and it becomes void if the owner breaks it.

The Treasurer runs Last Chance Payment Plan classes for owners seeking a third delinquent tax contract, online and at the Financial Empowerment Center at 2079 East 9th Street. Delinquent Tax Outreach is the unit that helps the Prosecutor and Treasurer collect overdue tax.

If you plan to sell with a balance owing, ring the Treasurer, learn the amount and ask whether a payment contract exists. The title company then has the full picture, and the tax can be paid out of your proceeds.

To contest a value, file a complaint with the Board of Revision any time from January 1 to March 31. The next filing period runs from January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027. A complaint must claim over-valuation, under-valuation, discriminatory valuation, illegal valuation or an incorrect determination of use.

The list of people allowed to file is long: any property owner in the county, the commissioners, the prosecutor, the treasurer, any school board in the county, and the mayor or legislative authority of a municipality with land in the county. The county was last reappraised in 2024, part of Ohio's six-year cycle, and a higher valuation alone does not guarantee a bigger bill.

Opinion alone will not carry a residential complaint. The board looks for documents such as:

  • A full appraisal report completed in the last calendar year
  • Dated photographs of the property's current condition
  • Certified contractor estimates for repairs
  • A purchase agreement with its closing statement
  • Certified new construction costs from the builder

Call the board at 216-443-7195. Its office is on the second floor at 2079 East Ninth Street, with weekday hours of 8:30 to 4:30. Each complaint is set for a hearing, so arrive with your evidence in hand. A recent buyer has an easy case to document, since the purchase agreement and closing statement are on the list.

The Fiscal Office's reappraisal page links four resources: the homestead exemption, an owner occupancy credit, a military deferment under which property taxes can be deferred, and Property Alerts to guard owners against deed fraud. Each has its own state form or sign-up, so ask the Fiscal Office which ones fit a house you own but do not live in.

At sale, the seller covers the conveyance fee from ORC 319.54: $1 or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is larger. Section 319.202 has the buyer file a statement of value, and any county transfer tax is added. In Cuyahoga County that step runs through the Fiscal Office's Transfer and Recording unit before the recorded copy is issued.

sections.h2: Before you list a Cuyahoga County house
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps the sale from stalling on paperwork:

  • Call the Treasurer at the Administrative Building for the balance on your parcel, including any contract in force.
  • Decide whether you want to contest your value. The filing window closes March 31, and a purchase agreement plus closing statement is accepted evidence.
  • Find out whether you hold a homestead exemption or owner occupancy credit, because the buyer's value statement asks.
  • Sign up for Property Alerts if the house will sit empty while it is listed.
  • Ask Transfer and Recording on the 4th floor what it needs for the deed.

Cash buyers usually close without a lender's review, yet the Treasurer's payoff and the conveyance fee are the same, so the preparation is the same too. Having these answers ready before the first showing lets you accept an offer without waiting days for county offices to respond, and it keeps the closing date from slipping.

Cuyahoga is a large urban county on the shore of Lake Erie, where the July 1, 2025 estimate is 1,232,925 residents, down 2.5% from 2020. It holds 616,777 housing units and 554,551 households, and 59.4% of homes are owner-occupied. A typical owned home is worth $195,400 on the 2020 to 2024 figures, and median rent is $1,060 a month. Builders pulled 1,896 permits in 2025. A countywide figure hides large gaps between Cleveland, the inner ring and the outer suburbs, so price a particular house from comparable sales or a written offer.

faqs.q: When is Cuyahoga County real estate tax due?
faqs.a: Mid-February and mid-August. The tax is billed in arrears, so taxes accrued in one year are payable the next.

faqs.q: When can I file a valuation complaint in Cuyahoga County?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. The next filing period runs from January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay my Cuyahoga County tax online?
faqs.a: Not for an electronic check. A debit card costs a flat $2.95 and a credit card costs 2.3% with a minimum of $1.50.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late real estate tax payment?
faqs.a: ORC 323.121 sets a ten percent penalty on the unpaid half, cut in half if the whole amount is paid within ten days. Interest is charged on delinquent taxes as well.

faqs.q: Can the county help if I cannot pay all at once?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer offers a delinquent tax payment plan and holds Last Chance Payment Plan classes for owners seeking a third contract. Call the Treasurer's Office to ask which plan fits.
